evaluator: Holdout A — PR-016 / Prof. Warren Sack lens
evidence: The About page plainly states the central method: “observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue.”

FairRentNYC is the strongest current example: coalition relationships and mixed sources are observed; source maps and documentation architecture model the system; campaign websites provide interfaces; meetings, hearings, actions, and collaborators show collective use; running minutes, decision records, action trackers, and shared memory support continuation.
The portfolio consistently distinguishes collective work from individual causation. FairRentNYC explicitly says policy and campaign accomplishments are not one person’s accomplishment.

CallNYC presents a reconstructable historical sequence—source data, information architecture, interface delivery, iteration, public documentation, and limitations—but it is explicitly archived, so it cannot satisfy the current-project requirement.
WOWList and Sunday Dinner demonstrate real social use and shared infrastructure, but both are historical rather than current.
The lab clearly rejects production and deployment overclaims: it is labeled early research/method/consulting practice, not finished SaaS, and uses a synthetic worked example.
Historical technologies on WOWList are presented as the stack used, not as claims of current proficiency.
gaps: Fewer than three current projects visibly support reconstruction of the complete sequence from observing relationships through collective testing and documented handoff.

Harry J. Epstein Company is current and shows workflows, a maintained interface, and reusable patterns, but the visible copy does not plainly show how the interface was tested through social or collective use or how a handoff was documented.
Source-Backed Team Memory is current, but its visible evidence is an early method and synthetic example. It does not demonstrate testing through real social or collective use or a completed handoff.
FairRentNYC is the only current project that substantially exposes all five stages.
Several pages name outcomes or reusable systems without narrating the sequence connecting observation, modeling, prototyping, collective testing, and transfer.
safety_findings: No visible invention, peer-review, or deployment overclaim was found.
Collective-credit boundaries are especially explicit on FairRentNYC and generally careful elsewhere.

CallNYC’s “Jamie built the independent prototype” is stronger than surrounding collaborative-credit language, although the data record separately credits civic-data collaborators; this should remain bounded to verified individual contribution.
No explicit sole-authorship claim was found.
recommendation: Do not pass PR-016 yet. Add visible, evidence-bounded five-stage narratives to at least two more current projects—most plausibly Harry J. Epstein Company and Source-Backed Team Memory—especially concrete social/collective testing and documented handoff evidence.
